This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V.Act') has been filed against award dated 17/05/2017 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Surajpur, District - Surajpur (CG) in Motor Accident Claim No.111/2016.

entities.label: COURT

2. By the impugned award, learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.1 lakh in favour of the claimants as compensation on account of death of their only daughter Khusbu Yadav in an unfortunate accident Sifal Yadav vs Branch Manager, The Oriental ... on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127303917/
1 that took place on 18/05/2016 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle (Scorpio)
bearing registration No.CG-15-B-9915 by driver-respondent 2, owned by respondent No.3 and insured with respondent No.1 / insurance company.

entities.text: Sifal Yadav vs Branch Manager, The Oriental
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claim application was resisted by the respondents on various grounds.
Learned Tribunal after framing issues, decided those issues in favour of the appellants / claimants and awarded compensation as stated above.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants submits that the law with regard to death of a child is no longer res integra in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kishan Gopal and anr. v. Lala and ors., (2014) 1 SCC 244 and Kurvan Ansari @ Kurvan Ali and anr. v.
Shyam Kishore Murmu and anr., (2022) 1 SCC 317.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and anr. v. Lala and ors., (2014) 1 SCC 244
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Kurvan Ansari @ Kurvan Ali and anr. v.
Shyam Kishore Murmu and anr., (2022) 1 SCC 317
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that apart from this, the amount of compensation on other heads is also on the lower side.
4. Learned counsel for insurance company supports the award passed by the learned Tribunal and submits that looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, just compensation has been awarded.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the records.

6. In the light of judgments passed in the case of Kurvan Ansari (supra) and Kishan Gopal (supra),
this Court feels that ends of justice would be served by awarding Rs.5 lakhs to the appellants /
claimants.

7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed and amount of Rs.5 lakhs is awarded to the appellants /
claimants.
After deducting Rs.1,00,000/- as awarded by learned Tribunal, enhancement comes to Rs.4,00,000/-.
Respondent No.1/ insurance company shall pay the amount of Rs.4,00,000/- within a period of 60 days with 6% interest from the date of claim application.

8. On enhanced amount of compensation being deposited, Rs.1,75,000/- (each) shall be invested as fixed deposit in the name of appellants / claimants No.1 and 2 in a Nationalised Bank for the period of 2 years.

Remaining amount shall be paid to claimant / appellant No.2 by Bank transaction /
account payee cheque.

Sd/-
(Sachin Singh Rajput ) Judge Deepti Sifal Yadav vs Branch Manager, The Oriental ...
